name: Specter ID Spoofer — 'Janus Mask'
description:
The Janus Mask is an identity spoofing platform developed by Zheng-Dao Bioelectric, built around a thin-film facial overlay combined with a deep-stack signal emitter concealed in a collar insert or subdermal implant housing. The overlay — a breathable, skin-toned membrane that adheres to the face via electrostatic bonding — contains a network of micro-LED filaments capable of dynamically reshaping the apparent contours of the wearer's face to match a stored biometric profile. The effect is not cosmetic surgery; at conversational distance and under scrutiny it reads as unconvincing. But to a facial recognition camera operating at standard resolution and standard distance, it presents a statistically convincing alternate identity.

The signal layer handles the rest: the collar emitter broadcasts a spoofed biometric handshake packet that matches the loaded identity profile, feeding false retinal pattern data, gait metrics, and voiceprint signatures to passive scanning infrastructure. Meridian 88's ubiquitous street-level ID sweep systems — the kind embedded in transit nodes, commercial entrances, and public plaza cameras — rely on exactly this passive handshake architecture, making the Janus Mask highly effective at moving through urban space under a false name. The mask's biometric library can store up to twelve distinct identities, loadable via a dedicated app that Zheng-Dao officially markets for 'entertainment and theatrical performance applications.'

The Janus Mask occupies a peculiar position in Meridian 88's underground economy. It's expensive, technically sophisticated, and unambiguously illegal in every administrative zone, yet it circulates with relative openness among a certain class of professional because the people most motivated to crack down on it — corporate security and city enforcement — use functionally identical systems themselves under different product names.

cultural_context: In a city where your biometric data is constantly harvested, traded, and weaponized, the Janus Mask represents a form of radical identity sovereignty that resonates far beyond professional criminal circles. There are activists and privacy advocates who use them simply to move through the city as unrecorded persons — a political act as much as a tactical one. The masks have appeared in underground art installations and protest imagery, the hollow face rendered as a symbol of resistance to Meridian 88's surveillance architecture. Zheng-Dao has never publicly acknowledged the device's actual use case.
known_users: protection-program clients on the run from prior employers
story_hooks: A player's registered biometric profile begins appearing in places they've never been — someone is running their identity on a Janus Mask, and whatever that person is doing is accumulating a very bad record.

A contact offers a loaded Janus Mask with twelve pre-built identities as payment. One of the identities belongs to someone who is supposedly dead. Another belongs to someone very much alive who would pay significantly to know their biometrics had been compromised.

Zheng-Dao's theatrical app receives a forced update that quietly bricks all active Janus Masks in the field simultaneously — and someone in the network needs to know why, and who ordered it, before midnight.
